Job Description

Work Arrangement:
Please note that this position will be based on the Stanford campus and will be considered hybrid with the expectation to be on campus on average three (3) days per work week depending on events. In addition, this position may require working evenings and weekends.

Budgeted Salary:
The budgeted base salary range for this position is $113,212 – 120,000 per annum.

Stanford Live presents a wide range of the finest performances from around the world, fostering a vibrant learning community and providing distinctive experiences through the performing arts. With its primary home at Bing Concert Hall and a popular second venue at historic Frost Amphitheater, Stanford Live is simultaneously a public square, a sanctuary, and a lab, drawing on the breadth and depth of Stanford University to connect performance to the significant issues, ideas, and discoveries of our time.

The Director of Philanthropy is a bold individual with an entrepreneurial approach to building out Saban Community Clinic’s (SCC) major gift fundraising program. They will forge authentic, trust-based relationships that align donor interests with SCC’s mission and growth priorities.
This role is for a relationship builder and proven closer
—someone who doesn’t wait for opportunities, but actively creates them. The ideal candidate is an authentic connector and a strategic prospector: equally skilled at opening new doors, identifying untapped donor potential, and converting relationships into transformational philanthropy.

Reporting to the Chief Marketing & Advancement Officer, this role will help shape and scale SCC’s major gift program by expanding the donor base, unlocking “hidden gems” within the database, and introducing new ideas, partnerships, and pathways for giving.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Develop and execute an ambitious major gifts strategy with clear, measurable revenue goals
Actively builds and cultivates a portfolio of high-net-worth individual donors and family foundations with an emphasis on 5,6, and 7 figure gifts
Proactively build a pipeline - sourcing and engaging new major donor prospects through networking, referrals, events, and creative outreach strategies
Mine and analyze the donor database to identify under-engaged supporters and “hidden gems” ready for deeper investment
Identify and pursue new opportunities for additional philanthropic investment, including new initiatives, partnerships, and/or campaigns.
At the direction of the CMAO, manages donor communications, appeals and social media, related to fundraising and engagement building collateral.
Represents SCC at various community events, inter-agency meetings, and special events, as needed.
Collaborates with SCC’s Executive Team, the Board of Directors, the Board of the Friends of SCC to identify, cultivate, solicit and steward donors.
Collaborates with the CMAO on annual and multi-year strategic fundraising plans, which may include annual and capital campaigns, the planned giving program and fundraising events.
Documents donor interactions in Salesforce database, including all communication points, gift data entry, report generation, bulk mailings, donor gift acknowledgment, stewardship, and grant tracking.
Other duties as assigned by CMAO, including management of team members as assigned.

Position Requirements:

Bachelor’s level degree preferably marketing, nonprofit management, communications or related discipline and several years of experience in increasingly responsible positions. Advanced degree and/or certification professional preferred. Experience in health care or equivalent sectors preferred, but not required
7+ years of experience in major gifts or comparable front-line fundraising roles
Demonstrated success closing significant gifts and managing a large portfolio (5 –7 figure gifts)
Proven instincts and ability to build a donor pipeline
, including identifying, qualifying and securing new donors
Extensive experience leveraging donor database and CRM systems (Salesforce NPSP and/or Raiser’s Edge) to drive data-informed fundraising strategy and enhance donor engagement and reporting.
Track record of converting relationships into philanthropic investment through thoughtful, strategic engagement
Proficiency in Planned Giving vehicles a plus
Deep expertise in fundraising strategy and best practices, with a demonstrated record of driving significant philanthropic growth.
Demonstrated knowledge of best practices in fundraising marketing and communications for a mid-size nonprofit.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office and related productivity tools, with a strong understanding of relational databases and the strategic use of social media platforms to support engagement, communications, and fundraising objectives.
Very effective oral and written communications skills, including public speaking.
A working knowledge and experience in developing long-term relationships with organizations and companies that might provide support.

Actual salary offers are considered by various factors, including budget, experience, skills, education, licensure and certifications, and other business considerations. jobs.title: Managing Director of Enrollment
jobs.description:
About Us

Brilla Schools, a growing K-8 network in the Bronx, serves over 2,000 students with plans to expand to educate 3,000 across four elementary and four middle schools. Managed by Seton Education Partners, Brilla Schools are dedicated to forming students of strong wisdom and virtue. Our classically inspired approach to education combines a content-rich curriculum, inquiry-driven learning, and a focus on virtues, while providing individualized support to meet each child's unique needs. A national leader in character education and supporting students with varying needs, over the past two years, Brilla alumni have secured spots in the most prestigious high schools in the tri-state area, earning over $3 million in scholarships and financial aid. Our staff are mission-aligned change-makers who believe in fostering a joyful, rigorous learning environment, and Brilla offers some of the most competitive salaries in the market to honor their dedication. With high expectations and a supportive community, we're preparing students to excel in high school, college, and beyond.

Position Overview

Brilla Schools seeks a mission-driven, results-oriented leader to serve as Managing Director of Enrollment for the Brilla Schools Network in the Bronx. The Managing Director of Enrollment will own and execute the network-wide recruitment, enrollment and retention strategy across elementary and middle school portfolios, ensuring Brilla meets ambitious growth, retention, and compliance goals while delivering an exceptional, family-centered enrollment experience.

This role is ideal for a strategic, data-driven leader with deep marketing and enrollment operations experience who can both set vision and build durable systems, while coaching and developing a high-performing team. The Managing Director of Enrollment reports to the Chief of Staff and partners closely with school leaders, operations, data, marketing, and external vendors

This role owns a department or function across the network, including strategy, systems, and performance outcomes. The Managing Director of Enrollment designs and implements processes that drive quality, equity, and consistency, manages Managers and/or team leads, and uses data and stakeholder feedback to improve results. This leader ensures strong execution while building sustainable systems for growth.

The Managing Director of Enrollment provides strategic leadership, systems ownership, and people management for all enrollment and retention efforts across the Brilla Schools Network. This role ensures enrollment operations are compliant, efficient, data-informed, and family-centered, while driving consistent practices and strong results across campuses.

Core Competencies & Responsibilities

Enrollment Strategy & Network Oversight

Own and execute the network-wide recruitment and enrollment strategy across elementary and middle school portfolios.
Set annual and quarterly recruitment and enrollment goals in partnership with senior leadership.
Analyze full-funnel enrollment data including leads, applications, offers, yield, retention, attrition, discharges, and no-shows to forecast trends and proactively mitigate risk.
Monitor and manage the full enrollment funnel, ensuring strong follow-up, lead nurturing, and conversion practices.
Regularly evaluate enrollment initiatives and sunset low-impact strategies in favor of high-yield practices.

Enrollment Team Leadership & People Management

Serve as people manager for the network-wide enrollment team, including Enrollment Managers, Student Recruiter Coordinators, and dotted line manager of Enrollment Captains.
Set clear roles, expectations, performance metrics, and accountability structures.
Lead regular 1:1s, coaching sessions, and performance check-ins.
Identify skill gaps and coordinate onboarding, professional development, and training.
Foster a collaborative, mission-driven team culture aligned to Brilla norms and goals.
Make staffing recommendations, including role design, hiring needs, and organizational improvements.
Ensure appropriate coverage, workload balance, and clear escalation pathways across campuses.

Systems Ownership & Data Integrity

Serve as system owner for SchoolMint, HubSpot, ATS, PowerSchool, and all enrollment-related workflows.
Ensure systems are accurate, aligned, and efficient across platforms.
Oversee network-wide data hygiene, cleanup, deduplication, and integrity efforts.
Partner with Data and Operations teams to resolve system issues and streamline processes.
Leverage data to drive forecasting, decision-making, and leadership reporting.

Lottery & Compliance Management

Lead and oversee the annual enrollment lottery in full compliance with authorizer and state requirements.
Ensure correct prioritization, offer management, documentation, and communication timelines.
Maintain accountability for lottery setup, execution, and system readiness.
Train enrollment staff on lottery procedures and compliance expectations.

Retention Strategy & Oversight

Own and manage network-wide student retention strategies in partnership with campus leadership and enrollment captains.
Analyze attrition and discharge trends and identify root causes.
Develop and adjust campus-specific retention plans to minimize withdrawals.
Partner with school leaders to implement timely interventions for at-risk families.
Track retention metrics and integrate insights into seat planning and projections.

Enrollment Events & Campus-Based Recruitment

Design, standardize, and oversee high-impact enrollment events, including ACE events and New to Brilla events.
Establish clear goals, timelines, staffing plans, and success metrics.
Ensure events are family-centered, well-executed, and aligned to network priorities.
Evaluate outcomes and continuously refine event models to maximize conversion.

Family Engagement & Community Growth

Ensure enrollment practices are timely, equitable, and family-centered.
Oversee enrollment communications, outreach standards, and follow-up practices.
Guide open houses, tours, community-based recruitment, and neighborhood outreach.
Oversee Family Ambassador programs, Partner Parish outreach, and CBO partnerships.
Identify and remove systemic barriers to enrollment and retention.

Consultant & Vendor Management

Manage external recruitment, CRM, and enrollment and marketing consultants.
Serve as primary point of contact for HubSpot optimization consultants, translating enrollment needs into workflows and reporting.
Set scopes of work, timelines, deliverables, and success metrics.
Evaluate consultant effectiveness and ROI.

External Partnerships & Marketing Channels

Engage with external partners (billboards, subway, out-of-home advertising).
Identify and evaluate new marketing channels based on cost, reach, and yield.
Coordinate with marketing and operations teams to ensure alignment with brand and timelines.
Track campaign performance and make data-informed recommendations.

SOP Development & Operational Excellence

Own and approve Standard Operating Procedures for all enrollment processes (applications, lottery, transfers, discharges, withdrawals).
Ensure SOPs are documented, trained, and consistently implemented.
Identify inefficiencies and lead continuous improvement efforts.
Partner cross-functionally to strengthen workflows and execution.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Reporting

Serve as the primary enrollment liaison to senior leadership.
Provide regular enrollment updates, projections, and risk assessments.
Partner with campus leaders to align enrollment strategy with school culture and capacity.
Support leadership decision-making with clear, actionable insights.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required
5+ years of enrollment, operations, or school-based leadership experience
Experience managing teams and coaching staff
Strong proficiency in Google Suite, Excel, and data systems
Experience with SchoolMint, PowerSchool, ATS, HubSpot, or similar platforms strongly preferred
Fluency in Spanish is a plus
Demonstrated ability to quickly build productive and meaningful relationships with multiple stakeholders including school and network based staff, families, and community members
Proven ability to effectively support, collaborate, and partner with a variety of personalities and working styles and an openness and generosity of spirit in navigating differences
A strong capacity to coach and develop others, providing guidance and support to ensure operational excellence and compliance across the network
Project management expertise and the ability to drive efficiency and excellence in all aspects of work alongside and/or through others
Optimistic self-starter with the ability to prioritize competing goals, exhibit flexibility, grace and sound judgment along with productive urgency in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment
Ability to leverage data to drive operational decisions, identify trends, and implement strategic improvements to enhance overall effectiveness and compliance across the network.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical and creative problem-solving skills
Flexible and willing to perform other duties as assigned
Ability to travel approximately 10-20% of the time, primarily within the US

Benefits

At Brilla Schools, we celebrate the unique skills, experiences, and passions that each staff member brings to our mission. To support their work, we offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package to provide competitive and adaptable coverage. We are committed to offering a benefits portfolio that supports the holistic health and wellness of our team members including:

Comprehensive Professional Development
: More than 225 hours annually, featuring two weeks of onboarding, coaching, and targeted training sessions to ensure staff excel in their roles and flourish.

Community and Culture
: An intentionally joyful workplace with over 30 bonding events each year, fostering connection and collaboration among staff and families in the Bronx.

Flexible Health Coverage
: A full suite of medical, dental, and vision plans designed to support diverse needs, utilizing Cigna and Anthem provider networks.

Competitive Compensation
: A salary range of $120,000 to $140,000, with pay varying within this range based on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Retirement Plans
: A 403(b) plan and 401(k) retirement options with matching contributions, helping you secure your financial future while you grow with us.

Work-Life Balance
: Generous paid time off, including all Federal Holidays and extended breaks, and wellness resources to support personal renewal and sustained excellence.

At Brilla, your dedication fuels our mission, and we're here to invest in your growth, well-being, and success—from recruitment to retirement!

Job Title:
Director of Operations
Reports To: Executive Director
Status: Full-Time, Exempt
Pay Range: $70,000-$80,000 /annual
Expected Start Date: Rolling

Position Description

BCFM is seeking an experienced operations leader who combines strategic thinking with practical execution. The ideal candidate will be a collaborative builder who can strengthen organizational systems while honoring the relationships, entrepreneurial spirit, and community-centered culture that have shaped BCFM for nearly 40 years. You may be a strong fit if you are a:

Nonprofit Operations Leader :
You have experience managing the systems, processes, and infrastructure that allow mission-driven organizations to grow effectively. You understand the realities of balancing limited resources, ambitious goals, and community expectations.

People-Centered Manager :
You believe strong organizations are built through strong teams. You have experience supporting managers, improving workplace culture, developing staff, and creating environments where people can do their best work.

Systems Builder: You enjoy turning complexity into clarity. You know when to create structure, when to simplify, and when to preserve flexibility. You have experience implementing practical systems that people actually use.

Collaborative Partner :
You build trust across departments and functions. You understand that operations is a service function — creating the conditions for programs, fundraising, partnerships, and community impact to succeed.

Mission-Aligned Leader: You are motivated by BCFM’s mission to build a thriving local food system and believe in the power of farmers markets, local agriculture, food access, and community connection to create a better future.

Core Responsibilities

The Director of Operations will serve as a key member of Boulder County Farmers Markets’ leadership team, partnering closely with the Executive Director, Director of Finance, and Director of Marketing & Development to strengthen the systems, structures, and culture that will support BCFM’s next era of growth.

This is a builder role for an experienced nonprofit operations leader who enjoys creating clarity where complexity exists. The Director of Operations will bring thoughtful systems, strong people leadership, and operational discipline to an organization that has grown quickly through creativity, entrepreneurship, and deep community commitment. The Director of Operations will:

Build Organizational Infrastructure & Operational Systems

Develop and strengthen the internal systems, processes, and tools needed to support a growing nonprofit organization.
Translate organizational goals into practical workflows, timelines, accountability structures, and decision-making processes.
Lead efforts to improve operational efficiency, cross-team communication, documentation, and organizational alignment.
Establish scalable systems that allow staff to spend more time advancing mission impact and less time navigating operational barriers.
Build long-term partnerships with key stakeholders, including City and Boulder County partners, to ensure smooth operations

Lead People Operations & Organizational Culture

Serve as a trusted partner to staff and leadership on organizational culture, communication, and team effectiveness.
Oversee human resources functions, including policies, employee lifecycle processes, performance management, compensation practices, onboarding, and professional development.
Support managers in becoming stronger leaders through coaching, clear expectations, and consistent management practices.
Help cultivate a workplace culture grounded in collaboration, accountability, equity, and care.

Support Program Operations & Team Alignment

Partner with program leaders across Seasonal Markets, Food Hub, Food Access, and Community Programs to strengthen operational planning and execution.
Create structures that support coordination across year-round and seasonal teams.
Improve annual planning, budgeting processes, staffing models, and resource allocation.
Identify opportunities to simplify systems and eliminate unnecessary complexity.

Strengthen Financial & Administrative Operations

Partner with the Director of Finance and Executive Director to strengthen financial systems, reporting rhythms, and operational decision-making.
Support effective budgeting, forecasting, and resource planning across program departments.
Ensure administrative systems are aligned with organizational growth and future needs.

Prepare BCFM for Its Next Chapter of Growth

Help build the organizational foundation and systems needed to support year-round local food access, expanded fundraising, increased community engagement, and the potential development of a year-round market and community hub.

First-Year Priorities

1.
Build the Operational Foundation for Growth
: Create the systems, structures, and rhythms that help a growing organization operate with greater clarity and effectiveness.

2. Strengthen People Systems & Leadership Capacity:
Help BCFM evolve from a highly entrepreneurial organization into a sustainably managed organization.

3. Improve Cross-Department Coordination
: Create stronger alignment between programs, operations, finance, fundraising, and community engagement.

4.Partner in Building a Sustainable Future
: Help prepare BCFM for continued impact, including future facilities and program growth. In the first year, the Director of Operations will:

Who Thrives in This Role

The Director of Operations role is ideal for a leader who enjoys building. You are energized by the opportunity to bring structure, clarity, and sustainable systems to an organization with a strong mission, talented people, and significant momentum.

You thrive in environments where:
The vision is clear, but the systems to support that vision are still being built.
Creativity, entrepreneurship, and flexibility are valued alongside accountability and operational excellence.
You can move between strategy and execution — helping shape big-picture direction while also improving the day-to-day systems that make the work possible.
Relationships matter. You understand that strong operations are built through trust, communication, and partnership.
You enjoy solving problems, simplifying complexity, and creating tools that help others succeed.

This role will be especially rewarding for someone who has worked in a growing nonprofit, social enterprise, community organization, or mission-driven business and understands the unique challenge of building infrastructure while continuing to deliver meaningful impact.

Required Qualifications

7+ years of progressive experience in nonprofit operations, administration, organizational management, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience building and improving organizational systems, processes, and infrastructure.
Experience managing and developing staff, including supporting managers and building healthy team culture.
Strong understanding of nonprofit operations, including human resources, budgeting, planning, compliance, and organizational systems.
Experience successfully leading change, improving workflows, or helping organizations grow.
Excellent communication, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on implementation.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a nonprofit organization, social enterprise, community-based organization, food system organization, or similarly mission-driven environment.
Experience supporting organizations through periods of growth or transition.
Experience with organizational assessment, process improvement, or change management.
Familiarity with nonprofit financial management, fundraising operations, and board relationships.
Experience with event management and  managing seasonal, part-time, or distributed teams.
Passion for local food systems, agriculture, community development, or equitable access to healthy food.

Application Instructions

Applicants are encouraged to submit their resume and a cover letter summarizing interest in the position and relevant skills and experience to Mackenzie Sehlke at director@bcfm.org.
No phone calls please. Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis until the role is filled..

Compensation and Benefits

jobs.description:
Employment Type:
Full time Shift:

Description:
Mercy Care Atlanta is for a dynamic and transformational executive to serve as its next Chief Operating Officer.

Position Purpose

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the senior executive responsible for leading and optimizing day-to-day operations across multiple clinic sites in Atlanta and Chamblee, GA. Reporting to the Mercy Care Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the COO serves as a strategic advisor to the CEO helping to drive key organizational priorities, enhance operational effectiveness, and ensure alignment with Mercy Care’s mission and strategic direction. The COO also acts as a liaison across executive leadership, coordinates special initiatives of the CEO, and oversees the efficacy of the Office of the CEO.

Mercy Care:

Mercy Care is a nonprofit community health organization that provides primary care, dental, vision, behavioral health, pediatric and pharmacy services for underserved populations, especially people who are uninsured, underinsured experiencing homelessness or poverty.  It is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) and has a 340B Pharmacy.

Mercy Care supports the comprehensive needs of its patients providing extensive social supports this includes case management, substance abuse counseling, recuperative care individuals being discharged from the hospital, intensive supports for high utilizers of emergency departments of local hospitals. Mercy Care has been serving Atlanta since 1985.  

Mercy Care Mission:
 Furthering the healing ministry of the Sisters of Mercy, Mercy Care gives tangible expression to Christ’s merciful love by promoting health and health equity and providing compassionate, clinically excellent healthcare in the spirit of loving service to those in need, with special attention to the poor and vulnerable. 

Mercy Care Vision:
 Mercy Care will provide affordable, compassionate and excellent care to its patients, leading to improved health. Mercy Care will facilitate patients’ access to a network of social services and will stand with them in advocating for their own needs and for a health system that respects and serves all people. 

COO Key Responsibilities

Operational Leadership & Multi-Site Management
Oversees all clinic operations across the four-site clinic network to ensure efficient, high quality and consistent service delivery across locations. Works closely with the Director of Clinic Operations (direct report) who in turn manages individual clinic managers in various locations
Responsible for all facilities management. Works closely with the Director of Facilities in managing all medical and administrative office space across the four clinics
Supports the operations of the Executive Office, including priority tracking, and follow-up on action items
Facilitate cross-departmental collaboration to ensure alignment with organizational goals and strategic direction, Mercy Care values and healthcare standards
Coordinates high-level projects and interdepartmental initiatives, particularly those involving the executive team
Responsible for all aspects of IT management and strategy working closely with the IT staff and external consultants.
Leads, mentors and supports executive departmental leaders to enhance leadership capabilities and effectiveness in implementing strategic direction and vision of the CEO

Strategic & Executive Leadership
Serves as trusted thought partner to the CEO, monitoring and engaging with strategic planning implementation, decision-making, and execution of key initiatives.
Monitors progress toward institutional goals and mission-related objectives, ensuring accountability and timely outcomes.
Prepares and briefs the CEO on critical internal matters, including system-level initiatives, executive team coherence and major initiatives as assigned by the CEO.

Social Care & Street Medicine
Responsible for the oversight and strategic direction of the Social Care and Street Medicine teams. Works closely with the Director of Social Care & Street Medicine (DSC&SM) to manage the execution of the social care strategy ensuring proper coordination with various service lines.
Together with DSC&SM, ensure proper alignment of the social care strategy and the Mercy Care strategic plan and monitor, evaluate and recommend changes to the scope of social determinants addressed by the social care and street medicine teams.

Board & Stakeholder Engagement
Supports CEO's engagement with the Board of Directors, foundation leaders, donors, sponsors, and Mercy Care representatives.
Supports the executive assistant with the coordination of board meeting logistics, materials preparation, and follow-up communications.
Represents the CEO and SJHS leadership in key internal meetings as needed.

Communications & Advocacy
Acts as a liaison between the CEO's office and internal departments, faith-based sponsors, civic leaders, and community organizations as needed by CEO.
Supports advocacy and public policy efforts related to Mercy Care, urban health equity, and community wellness.

Qualifications

Master’s degree in healthcare administration, Business Administration, Public Health, or a Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited institution.
Experience: Minimum of 10 to 15 years of progressive leadership experience, preferably in healthcare, nonprofit management, or government. Prior experience working within a mission-driven nonprofit institution is strongly preferred. Experience managing cross functional teams and organizational change initiatives in complex settings.

Demonstrated success in strategic planning implementation, operational execution and change management.

Skills & Attributes: Strong management and leadership skills. Strong strategic thinking and project management capabilities. Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. High emotional intelligence, discretion, and sound judgment. Ability to build consensus, foster collaboration, and navigate organizational complexity.

More About Mercy Care:

In 2025, Mercy Care saw over 18,000 individual patients in over 70,000 visits. 
66% were experiencing or at risk of homelessness 

58% were uninsured 

98% had incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level  

Annually Mercy Care must raise $15-$20 million, manage investment income and complex federal and state grants while maximizing patient revenue wherever possible. To do its work, Mercy Care owns the buildings that host its two large clinics, a fleet of vehicles and mobile clinics and is a 20% owner of the affordable housing development on its downtown campus. Mercy Care recently adopted and Trinity Health approved a 3-year strategic plan—The Conspiracy of Compassion-- that will increase patient care by 25%, improve the quality of care delivered while building a model for serving complex patients that others in Trinity Health and across the country can replicate. 

Mercy Care employs a whole person approach to healthcare, putting the individual at the center and addressing not just their immediate and long-term health needs but the underlying social and economic issues that might be making it difficult for them to stay healthy.  This model of care is rooted in the research that an individual’s health is only partially influenced by healthcare and is far more affected positively or negatively by the physical environment, lack of access to basic goods and services and reduced educational and economic opportunities. While the model is based on data and scientific evidence at its core, Mercy Cares strives to ensure that every patient feels welcome, loved and accompanied on their journey.

Our Commitment

Rooted in our Mission and Core Values, we honor the dignity of every person and recognize the unique perspectives, experiences, and talents each colleague brings. By finding common ground and embracing our differences, we grow stronger together and deliver more compassionate, person-centered care. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. Raritan Headwaters Association (RHA) is seeking an experienced, relationship-driven Development Director
to lead and grow the fundraising program of one of New Jersey’s leading watershed conservation organizations.
This is an opportunity for a seasoned development professional to step into a senior leadership role with significant autonomy, strong organizational support, and a compelling mission. Working closely with the Executive Director, Board of Trustees, and a talented staff team, the Development Director will help shape RHA’s next phase of growth and deepen the relationships that sustain our work to protect clean water, natural lands, and healthy communities.
About Raritan Headwaters

RHA protects the water and natural resources of New Jersey’s 470-square-mile Upper Raritan River watershed, spanning 38 municipalities across Hunterdon, Somerset, and Morris counties.
More than 300,000 people live within the watershed, and approximately 1.5 million people downstream depend on its water as a source of drinking water. From our headquarters at the 170-acre Fairview Farm Wildlife Preserve in Bedminster, RHA advances its mission through science, land preservation, restoration, education, advocacy, and community engagement.
Our work is ambitious, hands-on, and highly collaborative. The Development Director will join an organization with a strong reputation, an engaged Board and donor community, a multi-million-dollar annual budget, and significant opportunities to expand philanthropic support.
RHA is committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable organization and encourages candidates from all backgrounds to apply.
The Opportunity

The Development Director serves as RHA’s senior fundraising strategist and a key member of the organization’s leadership team.
The Director will lead a comprehensive development program that includes individual and major giving, foundations, corporate partnerships, planned giving, annual campaigns, and special events. A particular priority will be building deeper relationships with individual donors and expanding RHA’s major and planned giving programs.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys both strategy and relationships
: someone who can see the big picture, build a strong fundraising pipeline, and also genuinely enjoy sitting down with donors, introducing them to RHA’s work, and helping them find meaningful ways to support it.
The Development Director will have considerable opportunity to shape the program rather than simply administer an existing model.
What You’ll Do

Lead RHA’s fundraising strategy.

Develop and execute a comprehensive development plan that supports RHA’s strategic priorities and long-term financial sustainability. Identify opportunities to diversify and grow philanthropic revenue across individual giving, major gifts, foundations, corporations, and planned giving.

Use Raiser’s Edge and other tools to maintain a strong donor pipeline, track progress, identify opportunities, and inform fundraising decisions. Establish useful metrics and reporting without losing sight of the relationships behind the data.
Help tell RHA’s story.

A flexible, mission-driven work environment
The opportunity to work from RHA’s beautiful 170-acre Fairview Farm Wildlife Preserve

We aim to uplift investors, foster flourishing families, create enduring trust, and contribute to a more beautiful world through our investments, products and services, and new ventures.

Our investments are primarily in real estate, with additional allocations to tech, energy, and alternatives, employing a downside-protected, long-term approach to investing. We are grounded in timeless morals and seek to preserve and grow both investor capital and our own.

The Opportunity

Rex is seeking a Managing Director, Capital Markets to bring new ultra-high-net-worth investor relationships into the Rex ecosystem, with a mandate for $1M+ checks and a white-glove standard of service from first conversation through close. This is a principal-facing role for someone who can open doors that don't currently exist and turn them into durable capital partnerships. You will bring your own preexisting relationships and network of UHNW principals, family offices, and advisors to the table on day one, giving Rex immediate access to capital relationships the firm doesn't currently have. This role is anchored by three core mandates: originate, close, and steward. You will build a proprietary pipeline of UHNW principals, family offices, and their advisors who have not yet invested with Rex, drawing first on your own existing network and relationships, then expanding further through referrals and disciplined outreach rather than inbound. You will convert high-conviction conversations into committed capital across both deal-by-deal multifamily acquisitions and fund-level offerings, matching the right structure to the right investor. And you will deliver a white-glove experience that treats every principal relationship as a long-term partnership, not a transaction, building the trust that turns a first check into a decade of allocations. The ideal candidate brings 10 to 15+ years of experience as a seasoned capital raiser with a proven track record of sourcing and closing UHNW relationships at scale, along with an active, portable network of UHNW principals and family offices built over the course of their career, comfortable operating at the principal level and commanding credibility in rooms where trust is earned, not assumed. They combine polish with hustle: white-glove instincts paired with the grit to originate from zero. Fluency in real estate investment structures, deal-by-deal and fund-level alike, is essential, as is uncompromising discretion in handling sensitive investor relationships. This is not for order-takers managing inbound; it's for someone who builds the book from scratch. Must be missionary to the bone, driven by purpose as well as performance, and uncompromising in stewardship of investor trust. Fully remote.

About The Role

Rex is hiring a Managing Director, Capital Markets to expand its base of principal capital by building original relationships with UHNW investors, family offices, and their advisors, and converting those relationships into committed capital at scale. This person will bring a preexisting book of relationships and an active network to activate immediately, then build on that foundation with new origination over time.

This role owns outcomes across origination, structuring, and long-term stewardship, not just relationship management for an existing book. You will operate as the connective tissue between the investment team, deal structuring, and the principal, translating Rex's investment thesis and track record into conviction for investors who are meeting the firm for the first time.

You will build and run a disciplined outbound sourcing motion, beginning with your own network of UHNW principals and family offices and systematically identifying, engaging, and qualifying new relationships beyond it, rather than relying on inbound. You will match investors to the right vehicle, whether a single deal-by-deal acquisition or a fund-level commitment, and carry conversations from first touch through diligence to a closed, funded commitment. Who We Are

CIEE is a non-profit study abroad and intercultural exchange organization that transforms lives and builds bridges between individuals and nations through study abroad and international exchange experiences that help people develop skills for living in a globally interdependent and multi-cultural world.

Why work with us:  

You will change the world. CIEE builds bridges between people, countries, and cultures. We help young people participate in high-quality international exchange and study abroad programs that bring the world together. We change lives; our alumni change the world. Be part of the change!
You will receive a competitive total rewards package (only applicable for U.S. employees) .CIEE provides all employees with exceptional benefits offerings that increase total compensation by up to 25%. Our top-tier benefits include:
Paid time off and Parental leave
Gym Reimbursement Program
Employee Assistance Program
Short-term & Long-term Disability
6 floating Fridays (based on our eligibility rules)
CIEE Study Abroad Program discounts
403(b) Retirement Plan with employer contribution
Insurance Coverage (life, travel, medical, dental, and vision)
Flexible Spending Accounts/Health Savings Accounts (medical and dependent)
Voluntary Benefits (identity theft protection, pet insurance, accident, and critical illness)

You will be part of a fast-paced, international, and collaborative team of professionals. C IEE operates the largest nonprofit network of study abroad locations, with facilities and staff in over 30 countries. Additionally, we help international participants from over 140 countries come to the USA each year.  Committed to excellence and solving whatever problem the world throws at them, CIEE professionals work on international teams and are dedicated to advancing our almost 80-year-old mission to make the world a more peaceful place.

Who You Are

You are an experienced, resilient, and curious fundraiser who is equally comfortable opening new relationships and advancing established ones. You understand that discovery requires persistence, sound judgment, and the ability to distinguish genuine opportunity from polite interest. You are motivated by results, but you also know that sustainable fundraising is built through trust, disciplined followthrough, and strong internal collaboration,

What You’ll Do

Build and manage a growing portfolio of major and leadership gift donors and prospects, with an initial emphasis on discovery, qualification, and relationship development.
Conduct substantial proactive outreach to CIEE alumni and high-net-worth individuals who care about international education, including those with limited recent engagement with CIEE, and move promising relationships from initial contact to meaningful next steps and solicitation.
Prioritize and develop relationships with current donors who demonstrate potential for increased support, while also qualifying new prospects from CIEE's broader constituencies.
Develop and execute individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies that align donor interests with CIEE's established priorities and campaign goals.
Secure significant gifts and develop donors toward major-gift support, recognizing that a donor's first meaningful gift may be below CIEE's formal major-gift threshold.
Leverage the 80th anniversary and matching-gift opportunity to create timely, compelling pathways for engagement and giving while building relationships that extend beyond the campaign.
Prepare donor strategies, briefing materials, correspondence, proposals, and other materials tailored to donors' interests and decision-making needs.
Engage philanthropy leadership, executives, program leaders, alumni, board members, and other partners at the right moments in cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Use available wealth-screening, donor data, institutional knowledge, and research resources to identify, prioritize, and evaluate donor prospects.
Recommend strategic travel plans that maximize donor engagement and make responsible use of organizational resources.
Maintain timely and accurate donor records, contact reports, next steps, gift opportunities, and revenue forecasts in Salesforce.
Coordinate closely with annual giving and alumni engagement to support high[1]volume outreach, avoid conflicting communications, and transition responsive prospects into personalized relationship development.
Help establish and refine qualification, portfolio management, moves management, stewardship, travel, and donor-engagement practices in partnership with philanthropy leadership and operations.
Identify appropriate planned-giving, family foundation, donor-advised fund, corporate, or other opportunities that emerge through assigned relationships, coordinating with colleagues as needed.
Contribute to a collaborative fundraising culture in which relationship strategy and revenue credit reflect meaningful team contributions.

What You’ll Bring

The ideal candidate will possess:

Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Seven to ten years of progressively responsible fundraising experience preferred, including substantial experience with individual giving.
Proven track record of cultivating, soliciting, and closing significant gifts, including five- and six-figure commitments.
Demonstrated success initiating and developing donor relationships through proactive outreach, including relationships that were not previously qualified or fully developed.
Experience building or substantially expanding a donor portfolio rather than only managing a mature, inherited caseload.
Strong judgment in donor qualification, strategy development, solicitation timing, and the use of organizational leaders and partners.
Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, including comfort engaging high-net-worth individuals and navigating complex relationships.
Ability to work effectively in a team-based environment where several colleagues may contribute materially to a donor relationship or gift.
Strong organizational skills, disciplined follow-through, and comfort working toward clear activity, pipeline, and revenue expectations.
Experience using fundraising CRM systems; Salesforce experience is strongly preferred.
Comfort using donor data, wealth-screening results, and qualitative information to prioritize outreach without treating capacity alone as qualification.
An entrepreneurial and practical approach to building systems, testing strategies, and improving results in an evolving program.
A genuine interest in international education, cultural exchange, and CIEE's mission. Prior CIEE involvement is valued but not required.
Ability to work effectively across cultures and with people from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences.
Ability to embrace CIEE's Core Values: Excellence, Integrity, Respect, Inclusion, and Problem Solving.

CIEE believes that professionals with varied backgrounds bring unique approaches and ideas to solving problems and advancing our mission to bring the world together. Qualified candidates from underrepresented groups are strongly encouraged to apply.

Due to federal regulations and CIEE policies, a background check, reference check, and education and employment verification will be conducted as conditions of employment.

Position Description

BCFM is seeking an experienced operations leader who combines strategic thinking with practical execution. The ideal candidate will be a collaborative builder who can strengthen organizational systems while honoring the relationships, entrepreneurial spirit, and community-centered culture that have shaped BCFM for nearly 40 years. You may be a strong fit if you are a:

Nonprofit Operations Leader :
You have experience managing the systems, processes, and infrastructure that allow mission-driven organizations to grow effectively. You understand the realities of balancing limited resources, ambitious goals, and community expectations.

People-Centered Manager :
You believe strong organizations are built through strong teams. You have experience supporting managers, improving workplace culture, developing staff, and creating environments where people can do their best work.

Systems Builder: You enjoy turning complexity into clarity. You know when to create structure, when to simplify, and when to preserve flexibility. You have experience implementing practical systems that people actually use.

Collaborative Partner :
You build trust across departments and functions. You understand that operations is a service function — creating the conditions for programs, fundraising, partnerships, and community impact to succeed.

Mission-Aligned Leader: You are motivated by BCFM’s mission to build a thriving local food system and believe in the power of farmers markets, local agriculture, food access, and community connection to create a better future.

Core Responsibilities

The Director of Operations will serve as a key member of Boulder County Farmers Markets’ leadership team, partnering closely with the Executive Director, Director of Finance, and Director of Marketing & Development to strengthen the systems, structures, and culture that will support BCFM’s next era of growth.

This is a builder role for an experienced nonprofit operations leader who enjoys creating clarity where complexity exists. The Director of Operations will bring thoughtful systems, strong people leadership, and operational discipline to an organization that has grown quickly through creativity, entrepreneurship, and deep community commitment. The Director of Operations will:

Build Organizational Infrastructure & Operational Systems

Develop and strengthen the internal systems, processes, and tools needed to support a growing nonprofit organization.
Translate organizational goals into practical workflows, timelines, accountability structures, and decision-making processes.
Lead efforts to improve operational efficiency, cross-team communication, documentation, and organizational alignment.
Establish scalable systems that allow staff to spend more time advancing mission impact and less time navigating operational barriers.
Build long-term partnerships with key stakeholders, including City and Boulder County partners, to ensure smooth operations

Lead People Operations & Organizational Culture

Serve as a trusted partner to staff and leadership on organizational culture, communication, and team effectiveness.
Oversee human resources functions, including policies, employee lifecycle processes, performance management, compensation practices, onboarding, and professional development.
Support managers in becoming stronger leaders through coaching, clear expectations, and consistent management practices.
Help cultivate a workplace culture grounded in collaboration, accountability, equity, and care.

Support Program Operations & Team Alignment

Partner with program leaders across Seasonal Markets, Food Hub, Food Access, and Community Programs to strengthen operational planning and execution.
Create structures that support coordination across year-round and seasonal teams.
Improve annual planning, budgeting processes, staffing models, and resource allocation.
Identify opportunities to simplify systems and eliminate unnecessary complexity.

Strengthen Financial & Administrative Operations

Partner with the Director of Finance and Executive Director to strengthen financial systems, reporting rhythms, and operational decision-making.
Support effective budgeting, forecasting, and resource planning across program departments.
Ensure administrative systems are aligned with organizational growth and future needs.

Prepare BCFM for Its Next Chapter of Growth

Help build the organizational foundation and systems needed to support year-round local food access, expanded fundraising, increased community engagement, and the potential development of a year-round market and community hub.

Help BCFM evolve from a highly entrepreneurial organization into a sustainably managed organization.

4.Partner in Building a Sustainable Future
: Help prepare BCFM for continued impact, including future facilities and program growth. In the first year, the Director of Operations will:

Who Thrives in This Role

The Director of Operations role is ideal for a leader who enjoys building. You are energized by the opportunity to bring structure, clarity, and sustainable systems to an organization with a strong mission, talented people, and significant momentum.

You thrive in environments where:
The vision is clear, but the systems to support that vision are still being built.
Creativity, entrepreneurship, and flexibility are valued alongside accountability and operational excellence.
You can move between strategy and execution — helping shape big-picture direction while also improving the day-to-day systems that make the work possible.
Relationships matter. You understand that strong operations are built through trust, communication, and partnership.

Description:
Mercy Care Atlanta is for a dynamic and transformational executive to serve as its next Chief Operating Officer.

Position Purpose

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the senior executive responsible for leading and optimizing day-to-day operations across multiple clinic sites in Atlanta and Chamblee, GA. Reporting to the Mercy Care Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the COO serves as a strategic advisor to the CEO helping to drive key organizational priorities, enhance operational effectiveness, and ensure alignment with Mercy Care’s mission and strategic direction. The COO also acts as a liaison across executive leadership, coordinates special initiatives of the CEO, and oversees the efficacy of the Office of the CEO.

Mercy Care:

Mercy Care is a nonprofit community health organization that provides primary care, dental, vision, behavioral health, pediatric and pharmacy services for underserved populations, especially people who are uninsured, underinsured experiencing homelessness or poverty.  It is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) and has a 340B Pharmacy.

Mercy Care supports the comprehensive needs of its patients providing extensive social supports this includes case management, substance abuse counseling, recuperative care individuals being discharged from the hospital, intensive supports for high utilizers of emergency departments of local hospitals. Mercy Care has been serving Atlanta since 1985.  

Mercy Care Mission:
 Furthering the healing ministry of the Sisters of Mercy, Mercy Care gives tangible expression to Christ’s merciful love by promoting health and health equity and providing compassionate, clinically excellent healthcare in the spirit of loving service to those in need, with special attention to the poor and vulnerable. 

Mercy Care Vision:
 Mercy Care will provide affordable, compassionate and excellent care to its patients, leading to improved health. Mercy Care will facilitate patients’ access to a network of social services and will stand with them in advocating for their own needs and for a health system that respects and serves all people. 

COO Key Responsibilities

Operational Leadership & Multi-Site Management
Oversees all clinic operations across the four-site clinic network to ensure efficient, high quality and consistent service delivery across locations. Works closely with the Director of Clinic Operations (direct report) who in turn manages individual clinic managers in various locations
Responsible for all facilities management. Works closely with the Director of Facilities in managing all medical and administrative office space across the four clinics
Supports the operations of the Executive Office, including priority tracking, and follow-up on action items
Facilitate cross-departmental collaboration to ensure alignment with organizational goals and strategic direction, Mercy Care values and healthcare standards
Coordinates high-level projects and interdepartmental initiatives, particularly those involving the executive team
Responsible for all aspects of IT management and strategy working closely with the IT staff and external consultants.
Leads, mentors and supports executive departmental leaders to enhance leadership capabilities and effectiveness in implementing strategic direction and vision of the CEO

Strategic & Executive Leadership
Serves as trusted thought partner to the CEO, monitoring and engaging with strategic planning implementation, decision-making, and execution of key initiatives.
Monitors progress toward institutional goals and mission-related objectives, ensuring accountability and timely outcomes.
Prepares and briefs the CEO on critical internal matters, including system-level initiatives, executive team coherence and major initiatives as assigned by the CEO.

Social Care & Street Medicine
Responsible for the oversight and strategic direction of the Social Care and Street Medicine teams. Works closely with the Director of Social Care & Street Medicine (DSC&SM) to manage the execution of the social care strategy ensuring proper coordination with various service lines.
Together with DSC&SM, ensure proper alignment of the social care strategy and the Mercy Care strategic plan and monitor, evaluate and recommend changes to the scope of social determinants addressed by the social care and street medicine teams.

Board & Stakeholder Engagement
Supports CEO's engagement with the Board of Directors, foundation leaders, donors, sponsors, and Mercy Care representatives.
Supports the executive assistant with the coordination of board meeting logistics, materials preparation, and follow-up communications.
Represents the CEO and SJHS leadership in key internal meetings as needed.

Communications & Advocacy
Acts as a liaison between the CEO's office and internal departments, faith-based sponsors, civic leaders, and community organizations as needed by CEO.
Supports advocacy and public policy efforts related to Mercy Care, urban health equity, and community wellness.

Qualifications

Master’s degree in healthcare administration, Business Administration, Public Health, or a Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited institution.
Experience: Minimum of 10 to 15 years of progressive leadership experience, preferably in healthcare, nonprofit management, or government. Prior experience working within a mission-driven nonprofit institution is strongly preferred. Experience managing cross functional teams and organizational change initiatives in complex settings.

Demonstrated success in strategic planning implementation, operational execution and change management.

Skills & Attributes: Strong management and leadership skills. Strong strategic thinking and project management capabilities. Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. High emotional intelligence, discretion, and sound judgment. Ability to build consensus, foster collaboration, and navigate organizational complexity.

More About Mercy Care:

In 2025, Mercy Care saw over 18,000 individual patients in over 70,000 visits. 
66% were experiencing or at risk of homelessness 

58% were uninsured 

98% had incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level  

Annually Mercy Care must raise $15-$20 million, manage investment income and complex federal and state grants while maximizing patient revenue wherever possible. To do its work, Mercy Care owns the buildings that host its two large clinics, a fleet of vehicles and mobile clinics and is a 20% owner of the affordable housing development on its downtown campus. Mercy Care recently adopted and Trinity Health approved a 3-year strategic plan—The Conspiracy of Compassion-- that will increase patient care by 25%, improve the quality of care delivered while building a model for serving complex patients that others in Trinity Health and across the country can replicate. 

Mercy Care employs a whole person approach to healthcare, putting the individual at the center and addressing not just their immediate and long-term health needs but the underlying social and economic issues that might be making it difficult for them to stay healthy.  This model of care is rooted in the research that an individual’s health is only partially influenced by healthcare and is far more affected positively or negatively by the physical environment, lack of access to basic goods and services and reduced educational and economic opportunities. While the model is based on data and scientific evidence at its core, Mercy Cares strives to ensure that every patient feels welcome, loved and accompanied on their journey.

Our Commitment

Rooted in our Mission and Core Values, we honor the dignity of every person and recognize the unique perspectives, experiences, and talents each colleague brings. By finding common ground and embracing our differences, we grow stronger together and deliver more compassionate, person-centered care. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law.

new_jobs.description:
Company Overview

Rex is a privately held ecosystem of entrepreneurial ventures led by Peter Rex, spanning real estate private equity, technology, insurance, and AI. We build businesses and investment platforms that generate both exceptional financial returns and meaningful societal impact. At the core of our strategy is investor engagement: attracting aligned capital partners who share our long-term vision. We are building the most compelling investor-facing ecosystem in the private markets. The role offers exposure to a uniquely diverse platform, combining institutional-quality real estate and high-growth tech ventures, all aligned under a singular mission-driven vision.

About Us

Our mission is to catalyze human flourishing through stewardship, serving people in all nations. We seek a transcendent impact, second to none, crossing geographies and making a permanent mark on history.

We aim to uplift investors, foster flourishing families, create enduring trust, and contribute to a more beautiful world through our investments, products and services, and new ventures.

Our investments are primarily in real estate, with additional allocations to tech, energy, and alternatives, employing a downside-protected, long-term approach to investing. We are grounded in timeless morals and seek to preserve and grow both investor capital and our own.

The Opportunity

Rex is seeking a Managing Director, Capital Markets to bring new ultra-high-net-worth investor relationships into the Rex ecosystem, with a mandate for $1M+ checks and a white-glove standard of service from first conversation through close. This is a principal-facing role for someone who can open doors that don't currently exist and turn them into durable capital partnerships. You will bring your own preexisting relationships and network of UHNW principals, family offices, and advisors to the table on day one, giving Rex immediate access to capital relationships the firm doesn't currently have. This role is anchored by three core mandates: originate, close, and steward. You will build a proprietary pipeline of UHNW principals, family offices, and their advisors who have not yet invested with Rex, drawing first on your own existing network and relationships, then expanding further through referrals and disciplined outreach rather than inbound. You will convert high-conviction conversations into committed capital across both deal-by-deal multifamily acquisitions and fund-level offerings, matching the right structure to the right investor. And you will deliver a white-glove experience that treats every principal relationship as a long-term partnership, not a transaction, building the trust that turns a first check into a decade of allocations. The ideal candidate brings 10 to 15+ years of experience as a seasoned capital raiser with a proven track record of sourcing and closing UHNW relationships at scale, along with an active, portable network of UHNW principals and family offices built over the course of their career, comfortable operating at the principal level and commanding credibility in rooms where trust is earned, not assumed. They combine polish with hustle: white-glove instincts paired with the grit to originate from zero. Fluency in real estate investment structures, deal-by-deal and fund-level alike, is essential, as is uncompromising discretion in handling sensitive investor relationships. This is not for order-takers managing inbound; it's for someone who builds the book from scratch. Must be missionary to the bone, driven by purpose as well as performance, and uncompromising in stewardship of investor trust. Fully remote.

About The Role

Rex is hiring a Managing Director, Capital Markets to expand its base of principal capital by building original relationships with UHNW investors, family offices, and their advisors, and converting those relationships into committed capital at scale. This person will bring a preexisting book of relationships and an active network to activate immediately, then build on that foundation with new origination over time.

This role owns outcomes across origination, structuring, and long-term stewardship, not just relationship management for an existing book. You will operate as the connective tissue between the investment team, deal structuring, and the principal, translating Rex's investment thesis and track record into conviction for investors who are meeting the firm for the first time.

You will build and run a disciplined outbound sourcing motion, beginning with your own network of UHNW principals and family offices and systematically identifying, engaging, and qualifying new relationships beyond it, rather than relying on inbound. You will match investors to the right vehicle, whether a single deal-by-deal acquisition or a fund-level commitment, and carry conversations from first touch through diligence to a closed, funded commitment. Once closed, you will own the ongoing relationship, ensuring every touchpoint reflects a white-glove standard that turns a first-time investor into a repeat, referring partner.

This is a hands-on, principal-facing role for a senior capital raiser who has built a book from scratch before, brings a live network with them, and wants to do it again inside a platform with real scale and transaction velocity behind it.

Key Responsibilities

Activate your existing network of UHNW principals, family offices, and advisors to generate early capital conversations for Rex.
Build and execute a proprietary origination strategy targeting UHNW principals, single-family offices, and their advisors who have not previously invested with Rex, beyond your existing relationships.
Source new relationships through direct personal networks, warm referrals, and disciplined, high-quality outbound outreach.
Qualify prospective investors on capital capacity, investment appetite, and fit across deal-by-deal and fund-level structures.
Lead first conversations and ongoing dialogue with principals, translating Rex's investment thesis, track record, and current opportunities with clarity and conviction.
Structure and recommend the right investment vehicle for each investor, whether a specific multifamily acquisition or a fund-level commitment.
Drive the full capital-raising cycle for each relationship: outreach, education, diligence support, subscription, and close.
Own $1M+ check relationships personally, maintaining principal-level credibility and discretion throughout.
Deliver a white-glove investor experience at every stage, from first contact through post-close servicing and reporting.
Build long-term partnership plans for each principal relationship, aiming to convert a first commitment into repeat, multi-deal or multi-fund allocations.
Partner closely with acquisitions, asset management, and finance to ensure investors receive accurate, timely, and compelling information.
Track origination activity, pipeline conversion, and relationship health with disciplined CRM and reporting rigor.
Represent Rex at high-caliber investor events, conferences, and networking settings to expand the principal network.
Maintain uncompromising discretion and judgment in handling sensitive investor and financial information.

Ideal Candidate Profile

10-15+ years of experience in capital raising, private wealth, investment banking, or real estate investment management, with a demonstrated track record of sourcing and closing UHNW relationships at scale.
An active, portable network of UHNW principals, family offices, and advisors, with the credibility to bring those relationships into new conversations with Rex.
Proven ability to originate capital relationships from zero, without relying on an existing inbound book or handed-off relationships.
Comfortable operating at the principal level with UHNW individuals, family offices, and their advisors, commanding credibility and trust quickly.
Deep fluency in real estate investment structures, including both deal-by-deal LP equity and fund-level commitments.
Strong grasp of capital structuring, market trends, and investment strategy, able to communicate complex opportunities clearly to sophisticated investors.
White-glove relationship instincts: treats every investor interaction, regardless of size, as a long-term partnership rather than a transaction.
High personal network and demonstrated ability to convert relationships and referrals into committed capital.
Excellent judgment and uncompromising discretion in handling sensitive investor relationships and financial information.
Polished executive presence combined with genuine hustle and a willingness to originate relationships from scratch.
Highly organized, with the discipline to manage a complex, multi-relationship pipeline and report on it with rigor.
Missionary mindset: deeply aligned with Rex's mission and driven by purpose and stewardship of investor trust, not just performance.

Rex Ecosystem-Wide Mission

Catalyze Human Flourishing through our products and services and to elevate and further humanity in all our business dealings.

Rex Values / Rex Culture

Customer Fanatic. We fanatically focus on customers, seeking to ever-deliver more value, and inventing and innovating on their behalf.
Product/Service Passion. Our business thrives or dies by products and services.
Ludicrous Speed. Our default pace is extremely fast. Time is precious, life is short, and moving fast is more fun and effective.
FAWOMO. We will find a way, or make one.

Hardcore work hustle. Invictus mentality. Swagger with humility. Quiet professionalism. Thrifty and not materialistic. Loves who they work with, loves what they do, and loves who we serve.

new_jobs.description:
Roosevelt’s Work

The Roosevelt Institute takes on today’s greatest public policy challenges by advancing bold, cutting-edge research and policy ideas. We believe that the future of the American economy and our democracy depends on a new way of thinking about markets and government—and have successfully engaged with policymakers and the media to inform and shape public debate. Too few people hold too much economic and political power today, and we know that a stronger society is possible if we rectify this imbalance between private actors and the public. With a commitment to restructuring markets, transforming corporations, reviving democratic institutions, and reimagining the role of government, our work moves our nation toward a more resilient, equitable, and green future.

The Roosevelt Institute is a think tank, a student network, and the nonprofit partner to the Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum that, together, are learning from the past and working to redefine our collective future. Focusing on corporate and public power, labor and wages, and the economics of race and gender inequality, the Roosevelt Institute unifies experts, invests in young leaders, and advances progressive policies that bring the legacy of Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt into the 21st century.

What You’ll Do

Reporting directly to the President & CEO, the Executive Assistant and Board Liaison serves as the primary point of contact for internal and external constituencies on all matters pertaining to the office of the President. The Executive Assistant/Liaison enhances the CEO’s effectiveness by providing necessary executive support. The Executive Assistant/Liaison manages the CEO’s schedule, ensuring that her time is spent on matters of highest priority; liaises with the board of directors and executive team; organizes and coordinates CEO outreach and external relations efforts; supports the fundraising team; and oversees special projects.

The Executive Assistant/Liaison must be strategic, creative, and adaptable and enjoy working with a growing organization that is driven by mission, values, and results. This position requires the utmost professionalism in dealing with funders, board members, and other critical relationships for the Roosevelt Institute. The Executive Assistant/Liaison will have access to confidential information and must operate with great discretion. The Executive Assistant/Liaison must be consistent, well-organized, efficient, and mindful of their external/ambassadorial role and have a customer service–oriented mindset.

This is an individual contributing, nonmanagement, nonunion role.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Scheduling and Administrative Duties:

Manage the CEO’s calendar to ensure that priorities are properly elevated and that key relationships are stewarded. This will involve coordinating with multiple internal stakeholders, especially executive team members, and helping to enforce standards and decisions about calendar priorities.
Schedule meetings, speaking engagements, and travel to efficiently manage the CEO’s time
Ensure CEO is prepared for internal and external meetings, including coordinating briefing materials and agendas
Staff CEO at select meetings, including taking notes and helping ensure internal communication and follow-up
Track CEO action items and ensure priorities are moving
Draft and edit emails, documents, and presentations
Handle administrative work for the CEO, including receipts, contracts, and other financial and operational paperwork
Support special projects and initiatives as assigned by the CEO
Support Facilities team with DC office operations: oversee daily operations to ensure the space remains functional, clean, and well-stocked; coordinate visitor access, conference room scheduling, and security badge management; partner with Facilities, HR, and IT to address onsite needs and report maintenance issues promptly; and support new hire onboarding for DC-based staff, including workspace setup and office tours.

Board Liaison

Serve as the main point of contact for managing, facilitating, and coordinating logistics for all (c)(3) and (c)(4) Board–related meetings and events, including the budget and board member reimbursements. This includes facilitating and scheduling all committee meetings.
Serve as an administrative aide for the Board cochairs
Support the CEO and board leadership in preparation of Board materials for quarterly meetings
Take minutes and notes for full board and meetings, and ensure proper record retention and board governance.

What You’ll Have

Bachelor’s degree preferred
4–6 years relevant professional experience, with preference for someone who has supported a senior executive
Strong computer skills and experience with MS Office, Google suite of products, and social media web platforms; experience using Salesforce, Asana, or other database and project management tools a plus
Superior written and verbal communication skills
Demonstrated ability to work as part of a team, be flexible, and learn new skills quickly
Strong organizational skills that reflect ability to perform and prioritize multiple tasks and projects seamlessly with excellent attention to detail
Very strong customer service and interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships with stakeholders, including staff, board members, external partners, and donors
Demonstrated proactive approaches to problem-solving with strong decision-making capability
Emotional maturity and a sense of humor
Proven ability to handle confidential information with discretion, be adaptable to various competing demands, and demonstrate the highest level of customer/client service and response
Demonstrated ability to achieve high-performance goals and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
Ability to learn and work with existing systems and processes and suggest improvements as needed
Forward-looking thinking that actively seeks opportunities and proposes solutions
